actions.description:
Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Grab in its damage entry, or the monster has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect If used after a Strike, the monster attempts to [[/act grapple]] the creature using the body part it attacked with. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the creature's multiple attack penalty.

The monster can instead use Grab and choose one creature it's grabbing or restraining with an appendage that has Grab to automatically extend that condition to the end of the monster's next turn.
actions.name: Grab
actions.requirements: The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Grab in its damage entry, or the monster has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

actions.description:
The reef octopus emits a cloud of dark-brown ink in a @Template[emanation|distance:10]. This cloud has no effect outside of water. Creatures inside the cloud are Hidden and can't use their sense of smell. The cloud dissipates after 1 minute.

The octopus can't use Ink Cloud again for [[/br 2d6 #Recharge Ink Cloud]]{2d6 rounds}.
actions.name: Ink Cloud

actions.description: The reef octopus moves up to 80 feet in a straight line through the water without triggering reactions.
actions.name: Jet

actions.description: The reef octopus makes up to four arm Strikes with different arms, each against a different target. These attacks count toward the octopus's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after it makes all of its attacks.
actions.name: Writhing Arms

actions.description: The reef octopus can change the color of its skin to Hide even if it doesn't have cover.
actions.name: Camouflage

actions.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:17]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[1d4[poison]] damage and Off-Guard (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[1d6[poison]] damage and Off-Guard (1 round)

Stage 3 @Damage[1d8[poison]] damage and Off-Guard (1 round)
actions.name: Reef Octopus Venom

name: Reef Octopus
publicNotes: The common reef octopus is a risky but valuable catch for coastal fishers.
